privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.lede: Lesson Lab holds information about schools, staff, parents and children. This page explains what we collect, why, who can see it and the choices you have.

sections.title: 1. Who we are
paragraphs: Lesson Lab is a school management system for private schools in Saudi Arabia. In this policy, "we" means the Lesson Lab team, and "the service" means this website and the Lesson Lab app.

sections.title: 2. Our role and the school's role
paragraphs: When a school uses Lesson Lab, the school decides what data about its students, parents and staff is entered and why. The school is the data controller, and Lesson Lab processes that data only on the school's instructions, under an agreement with the school.
For the details visitors send us through this website, such as a demo request, Lesson Lab is the controller.

sections.title: 3. What we collect
items: Demo and contact forms: your name, school name, email, mobile number and your message.
School accounts: names, usernames, email addresses, roles and the school each user belongs to.
Records a school enters: for example classes, attendance, marks, fees and messages between teachers and parents.
Technical data: sign-in times, IP address, browser type and error logs, used to keep the service working and secure.

sections.title: 4. How we use it
items: To run the service for the school and its users.
To reply to demo requests and messages.
To send emails the service needs, such as sign-in codes and important notices.
To protect accounts, prevent misuse and fix problems.
paragraphs: We do not sell personal data, and we do not use student data for advertising.

sections.title: 5. Children's data
paragraphs: Student information is entered by the school, which is responsible for getting consent from parents or guardians where required. Parents see only their own children, and teachers see only the classes they teach.

sections.title: 6. Who we share it with
paragraphs: Each school's data is kept separate, and users of one school cannot see another school's data.
We use a small number of service providers, such as hosting and email delivery, who act on our instructions and must protect the data. We share data with authorities only when Saudi law requires it.

sections.title: 7. How we protect it
items: All traffic is encrypted with HTTPS.
Passwords are stored as one-way hashes, never as plain text.
School and platform administrators must use two-factor authentication.
Repeated failed sign-ins are blocked for a time.

sections.title: 8. Where it is stored and for how long
paragraphs: We aim to keep school data in Saudi Arabia, in line with the Personal Data Protection Law (PDPL).
We keep school data while the school uses Lesson Lab. When a school leaves, it can ask for an export, and we then delete its data unless the law requires us to keep it.

sections.title: 9. Cookies
paragraphs: We use only the cookies and browser storage the service needs, for example to keep you signed in, protect forms and remember your language. We do not use advertising cookies.

sections.title: 10. Your rights
paragraphs: Under the PDPL you can ask to see, correct or delete your personal data, or ask how it is used. If your data was entered by a school, please contact the school first; we will help them answer. You can also write to us directly.

sections.title: 11. Changes to this policy
paragraphs: If we change this policy, we will update the date at the top of this page and, for important changes, tell schools in advance.

story.title: Software that fits the school, not the other way round.
paragraphs: Most school software sold in this region is built for a different school system first, then translated. Fields get relabelled, but the week underneath still assumes a Monday start and a single calendar.
Lesson Lab is built around a Sunday–Thursday week, Hijri and Gregorian dates shown together, and Arabic as a first-class language throughout — not a toggle bolted on afterward.
It's early. We're working directly with a small number of pilot schools in Saudi Arabia to get the daily details right before opening up further.

items.title: Your data stays in Saudi Arabia
items.description: Records and backups are kept in-region, with a clear answer on where they live.

items.title: One record, every role

faq.q: Do you charge per student or per school?
faq.a: Per school, based on student count and modules you need — not a per-seat fee that punishes growth.

faq.q: Can we start with one grade before the whole school?
faq.a: Yes. Many schools pilot with a single grade or campus for a term before rolling out further.

faq.q: What happens to our data if we leave?
faq.a: You get a full export of your school's records. Nothing is held hostage in the system.
Yes — WhatsApp and email support both work in Arabic or English, whichever your staff prefer.
